endorsements.quote: To effectively combat such bias, models should be trained using multi-institutional datasets and surveyed for disparate performance during model deployment.

Empirical studies that holistically examine the integration of AI tools into care systems, their impact on patient outcomes, and broader systems-level outcomes are necessary to solidify the claim that AI can truly democratize care and enhance its accessibility and quality.

unlisted_practices: Validate AI algorithms carefully to ensure reproducible results before deploying them in other populations.
Invest in infrastructure for local validation and model recalibration in low- and middle-income countries.
Design digital health tools with lower technical requirements and cost, and enable mobile applications to work in both online and offline modes.
Establish national and international regulatory standards and a clear regulatory approval and deployment roadmap for AI models.
Adopt a multitiered approach to evaluate and address digital inclusion as a social determinant of health.
Develop a global consensus framework for ethical and equitable AI involving stakeholders from all global regions, including low- and middle-income countries.
Use reporting guidelines such as TRIPOD and DECIDE-AI to promote model transparency in AI research.
Map local settings and engage local stakeholders such as government agencies and NGOs in workflow design when implementing AI, especially in resource-limited settings.
Conduct economic evaluations and cost-effectiveness analyses of AI tools under different resource settings and set referral thresholds using health economic analysis.
Examine the impact of labor practices in AI development, including annotation of toxic content, to protect worker well-being.
Use privacy-preserving techniques such as homomorphic encryption, federated learning, synthetic data from GANs, and blockchain to protect patient data.
Apply cybersecurity measures such as user authentication, audit trails, data encryption, and secure data transmission to AI systems.
Standardize SDOH data collection, definitions, and terminologies to enable interoperability and multi-cohort validation of AI models.
Avoid unchecked, unaccounted, and untested applications of LLMs in clinical decision support.
Apply calibrated change management strategies when implementing digital health and AI.
Conduct research on factors that foster user trust in AI models and on explainability approaches usable by clinicians and patients.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/commentary article discussing the role, challenges, and ethical/responsible deployment frameworks for AI and LLMs in addressing social determinants of health.
